title: Who made it, sold it and ended it
lede: Titles are as given in the sources at the time. Later careers are included only where a source gives them.

people.name: Mark Lee
people.text: Described the research behind the product and defended it in 1995: “Our trial curve was so huge we almost hit 1.3 million barrels last year.”[^12]

people.name: Julie Demlow
people.text: Argued that the launch hype itself invited the backlash, and that the brand was still “a very respectable piece of business that is making the company a profit.”[^12]

people.name: Scott Rabschnuck
people.text: Spoke for the agency that made the television campaign and conceded that it had overdone the pitchman.[^12]

people.name: Roger Kabler
people.text: The comedian who played the man in the hat in the launch commercials.[^12]

people.name: Peter Coors
people.text: Told investors in mid-1995 that because Zima carried a higher margin, “the decline in volume compared to last year hurt our profitability through the second quarter.”[^12]

people.name: Jane Espenson
people.text: Mental Floss credits her with the name, chosen while working for the naming firm Coors hired.[^34]
people.later: Went on to write for television, including Buffy the Vampire Slayer.[^34]

people.name: Andy England
people.text: Signed off the withdrawal, citing weakness in the “malternative” segment and declining consumer interest.[^14][^15]

people.name: Dilini Fernando
people.role: Senior marketing manager for innovation, MillerCoors, 2018
people.text: Ran the second limited release: “people bought it by the case last year.”[^26]
